newsitem.title: UK: N.Sea crudes jump on buyer fear of July shortages.
newsitem.headline: N.Sea crudes jump on buyer fear of July shortages.

text.p: North Sea crudes were heavily traded on Friday at firmer numbers with absent Iraqi barrels forcing buyers to rush to cover July requirements, traders said.
Paper markets were also active and firm as bullishness overtook both the wet and cash crude trade.
"I think the sour market has been very tight for obvious reasons and that is now affecting the North Sea market," said one trader.

Osebergs traded at dated Brent +20 and +24 cents, 5-10 cents firmer on the day, a Gulfaks A moved at +3 cents, six cents better than on Thursday, a Flotta at -50 cents and a Draugen shifted at +40 cents.
Outright values were also boosted by the demand for July barrels and by fund buying, with August IPE contracts trading around $18.15 in the late afternoon in Europe.

Traders said that although Iraq had committed to restart crude exports, the hiatus between the last deliveries in late May and their resumption, anticipated some time in July, had inflicted a short-term tightness on the market.

Scepticism over Iraq's 10-day target for concluding an aid distribution deal with the U.N. and solving the logistical hurdles blocking exports was also forcing buyers to cover needs on a preventive basis.
"We are seeing big Iraqi contract holders coming into the market whereas normally they would not," one trader said.
Few non-Brent crude cargoes were now left available for July, he added.
"We've been a little bit surprised ourselves at the strength of the buying," said one seller. "It is unusual for the market to buy so far ahead."
